sources.note: The table ① draws, stored only on the manual path: "if not self.flash:" … "# causal mask to ensure that attention is only applied to the left in the input sequence", then a buffer holding "torch.tril(torch.ones(config.block_size, config.block_size))" - 1 on and below the diagonal, 0 above.

The three stages, in order: "att = (q @ k.transpose(-2, -1)) * (1.0 / math.sqrt(k.size(-1)))", then "att = att.masked_fill(self.bias[:,:,:T,:T] == 0, float('-inf'))" (the table cut to T × T; every 0 turns the score into −∞), then "att = F.softmax(att, dim=-1)" (per row, so −∞ becomes weight exactly 0).
Dropout on the weights comes next in training and is not modelled here: "att = self.attn_dropout(att)".

claims.statement: The mask sets every later score to −∞ before softmax, so those weights come out exactly 0.

sources.note: Scores and the multiplier in one line: "att = (q @ k.transpose(-2, -1)) * (1.0 / math.sqrt(k.size(-1)))" - every q·k score times one number, 1/√hs.
The mask runs after the multiply: "att = att.masked_fill(self.bias[:,:,:T,:T] == 0, float('-inf'))" - later positions become −∞ whatever the multiplier did to them.
Then "att = F.softmax(att, dim=-1)": −∞ gives weight exactly 0; the visible weights share 1.

claims.statement: Every score is multiplied by one positive number, 1/√hs, before the mask and softmax: a smaller multiplier gives flatter weights, a larger one sharper weights.

learner_intent.raw_user_message: What does softmax do to the scores?

claims.statement: Softmax exponentiates each score and divides by their sum, so every weight is positive and the weights add up to one.
Only the gaps between scores matter: bigger gaps give sharper weights, and equal scores give equal weights.
